The Salesforce Load connector supersedes the [Salesforce Query](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-query) connector, which is no longer available for new pipelines. Existing pipelines that use the Salesforce Query connector will continue to work as expected.

The Salesforce Load connector lets you connect to your Salesforce account and configure a query to load data from the Salesforce API. You can select the data source, choose the fields to include in your query, and apply filters to refine your results. You can also specify a row limit to control the number of records returned.The results of your query can be loaded into your destination as a new table or can replace an existing table. You can also configure incremental load settings to load only new or updated records since the last load.Your destination can be your connected cloud data warehouse or a cloud storage location. You can also configure advanced settings to control the output encoding, key sanitization strategy, and other options.

In Snowflake and Amazon Redshift projects, to write data to Salesforce instead of reading from it, use the [Salesforce Output](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-output) component.

If the component requires access to a cloud provider (AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud), it will use the [cloud credentials](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/guides/cloud-credentials) associated with your environment to access resources.To stage data to Azure Blob Storage, the Azure credentials associated with your environment must be assigned the `Storage Blob Data Contributor` role. For more information, read [User assigned with the Storage Blob Data Contributor role](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/1155139/user-assigned-with-storage-blob-data-contributor-r).

Salesforce IDs are shown in either a 15-character or 18-character format. The additional three characters form a checksum that allows the ID to function in case-insensitive systems. Both formats refer to the same record. Maia displays the 18-character version as returned by the Salesforce API.

### [​](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load\#connect)  Connect

[​](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load#param-connection)

Connection

drop-down

required

Select a [Connection](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/guides/connections). This connection defines all credentials needed to connect to the service.If the required connection doesn’t yet exist, you can create it here by selecting **Add Connection** in the drop-down. Read [Add a connection](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/guides/connections#add-a-connection) for further details, following that process from step 4 onwards. A connection created here is visible in the **Connections** tab and available for other connectors to use.A special value, `[Legacy connection]`, reveals additional properties that you can use to configure the connection directly in the component instead of selecting a pre-configured connection. This is primarily in place to maintain compatibility with older versions of the component which didn’t use the connection object mechanism, but it’s also available for use in new pipelines if you prefer this method.

The following properties in the **Connect** section of the component configuration are only visible if you selected `[Legacy connection]`. Otherwise, proceed to the [Configure](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load#configure) section.

[​](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load#param-authentication-type)

Authentication Type

drop-down

required

Choose to authenticate using either username and password, OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code, or OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials.For information about creating an OAuth connection for Salesforce, read the [Salesforce authentication guide](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/guides/salesforce-authentication-guide).

The Matillion-provided OAuth client is for convenience during the design phase and for testing. It isn’t supported for production workloads. For production workloads, use OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials with your own OAuth client.

You can also select **None** if you want to use the **Connection Options** property to authenticate.Choose your authentication type to reveal documentation for applicable parameters.

- OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code

- OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials

- **Yes:** Connect to a sandbox Salesforce account.

### [​](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load\#configure)  Configure

[​](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load#param-load-type)

Load Type

drop-down

required

- **Full Load:** Select this option to load your entire dataset.
- **Incremental Load:** Select this option to only load new and updated records from your dataset.

[​](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load#param-mode)

Mode

drop-down

required

- **Basic:** This mode will build a query for you using settings from the **Schema**, **Data Source**, **Data Selection**, **Data Source Filter**, **Combine Filters**, and **Row Limit** parameters. In most cases, this mode will be sufficient.
- **Advanced:** This mode will require you to write an SQL-like query to call data from the service you’re connecting to. The available fields and their descriptions are documented in the data model.

There are some special pseudo columns that can form part of a query filter, but are not returned as data. This is fully described in the data model.

While the query is exposed in an SQL-like language, the exact semantics can be surprising, for example, filtering on a column can return more data than not filtering on it. This is an impossible scenario with regular SQL.

[​](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load#param-data-source)

Data Source

drop-down

required

Select a single data source to be extracted from the source system and loaded into a table in the destination. The source system defines the data sources available. Use multiple components to load multiple data sources.

[​](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load#param-data-selection)

Data Selection

object selector

required

Select the columns to fetch from the selected data source. Only available in **Basic** mode.To use grid variables, toggle **Use Grid Variable** on. For more information, read [Grid variables](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/guides/grid-variables).

[​](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load#param-data-source-filter)

Data Source Filter

column editor

Define one or more filter conditions that each row of data must meet to be included in the load.

- **Input Column:** Select an input column. The available input columns vary depending upon the data source.
- **Qualifier:**
  - **Is:** Compares the column to the value using the comparator.
  - **Not:** Reverses the effect of the comparison, so “Equals” becomes “Not equals”, “Less than” becomes “Greater than or equal to”, etc.
- **Comparator:** Choose a method of comparing the column to the value. Possible comparators include: “Equal to”, “Greater than”, “Less than”, “Greater than or equal to”, “Less than or equal to”, “Like”, “Null”. Not all data sources support all comparators.
- **Value:** The value to be compared.

Toggle **Text mode** on at the bottom of the dialog to open a multi-line editor that lets you add items in a single block. For more information, read [Text mode](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/guides/components-overview#text-mode).To use grid variables, toggle **Use Grid Variable** on. For more information, read [Grid variables](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/guides/grid-variables).

[​](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load#param-sql-query)

SQL Query

code editor

required

Enter an SQL-like SELECT query to retrieve the data you want. This query must be written in the SQL accepted by your cloud data warehouse. Treat collections as table names, and fields as columns. Only available in **Advanced** mode.For more information, read the SELECT query documentation for your cloud data warehouse:

- [Snowflake](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/sql/select)
- [Google BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/query-syntax)

[​](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load#param-combine-filters)

Combine Filters

drop-down

The data source filters you have defined can be combined using either **And** or **Or** logic. If **And**, then all filter conditions must be satisfied to load the data row. If **Or**, then only a single filter condition must be satisfied. The default is **And**.If you have only one filter, or no filters, this parameter is essentially ignored.

[​](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load#param-row-limit)

Row Limit

integer

Set a numeric value to limit the number of rows that are loaded. The default is an empty field, which will load all rows.

[​](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load#param-high-water-mark-selection)

High-Water Mark Selection

drop-down

required

When **Incremental Load** is selected, select a datetime field from your dataset that is always updated when your data changes, such as `dateModified`. The connector will record the maximum value of this field each time you run this pipeline. On subsequent runs when **Incremental Load** is selected, only data with a higher value in this field will be loaded.

If no rows in the source have a higher value than the stored high-water mark, the task will complete with a “task is skipped” message. This is expected behavior, indicating that no new or updated data was found since the last successful run.

### [​](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load\#destination)  Destination

The Salesforce Load connector checks whether the destination table already exists—it doesn’t check whether the table contains data. What happens to an existing table depends on the **Load Strategy** parameter: **Fail if Exists** stops the pipeline rather than writing to the table, **Replace** or **Truncate and Insert** overwrite existing data, and **Append** adds to it without removing anything. The default option varies by warehouse.

- Snowflake

- Databricks

- Amazon Redshift

- Google BigQuery


[​](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load#param-destination)

Destination

drop-down

required

Select the destination for your data. This is either in Snowflake as a table or as files in cloud storage.

- **Snowflake:** Load your data into a table in Snowflake. The data must first be staged via Snowflake or a cloud storage solution.
- **Cloud Storage:** Load your data directly into files in your preferred cloud storage location. The format of these files can differ between source systems and will not have a file extension so we suggest inspecting the output to determine the format of the data.

When **Incremental Load** is selected, **Cloud Storage** is not supported as a destination.

- Snowflake

- Cloud Storage


[​](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load#param-warehouse)

Warehouse

drop-down

required

The Snowflake warehouse used to run the queries. The special value `[Environment Default]` uses the warehouse defined in the environment. Read [Overview of Warehouses](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/warehouses-overview.html) to learn more.

[​](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load#param-database)

Database

drop-down

required

The Snowflake database to access. The special value `[Environment Default]` uses the database defined in the environment. Read [Databases, Tables and Views - Overview](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/guides-overview-db) to learn more.

[​](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load#param-schema)

Schema

drop-down

required

The Snowflake schema. The special value `[Environment Default]` uses the schema defined in the environment. Read [Database, Schema, and Share DDL](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/sql-reference/ddl-database.html) to learn more.

[​](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load#param-table-name)

Table Name

string

required

The name of the table to be created in your Snowflake database. You can use a [Table Input](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/table-input) component in a transformation pipeline to access and transform this data after it has been loaded.

[​](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load#param-load-strategy)

Load Strategy

drop-down

required

Define what happens if the table name already exists in the specified destination. Only available when **Full Load** is selected.

- **Replace:** If the specified table name already exists, that table will be destroyed and replaced by the table created during this pipeline run.
- **Truncate and Insert:** Each time the pipeline runs, two operations are performed: first, the table is truncated, meaning all existing rows are deleted. Then, your new rows are inserted. The table itself is never destroyed and recreated.
- **Fail if Exists:** If the specified table name already exists, this pipeline will fail to run.
- **Append:** If the specified table name already exists, then the data is inserted without altering or deleting the existing data in the table. It’s appended onto the end of the existing data in the table. If the specified table name doesn’t exist, then the table will be created, and your data will be inserted into the table.

[​](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load#param-primary-keys)

Primary Keys

object selector

Select one or more columns to use as the table’s primary key. If you select multiple columns, the component creates a composite primary key using the combination of the selected columns.Leave this blank to create the table without a primary key.When using **Incremental Load**, if you select a primary key, the loaded data will be merged with your existing data. If you don’t select a primary key, the loaded data will be appended to your existing data.

[​](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load#param-clean-staged-files)

Clean Staged files

boolean

required

- **Yes:** Staged files will be destroyed after data is loaded. This is the default setting.
- **No:** Staged files are retained in the staging area after data is loaded.

[​](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load#param-stage-platform)

Stage Platform

drop-down

required

Use the drop-down menu to choose where the data is staged before being loaded into your Snowflake table.

- **Amazon S3:** Stage your data on an AWS S3 bucket.
- **Snowflake:** Stage your data on a Snowflake internal stage.
- **Azure Storage:** Stage your data in an Azure Blob Storage container.
- **Google Cloud Storage:** Stage your data in a Google Cloud Storage bucket.

[​](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load#param-internal-stage-type)

Internal Stage Type

drop-down

required

Select the Snowflake internal stage type. Use the Snowflake links provided to learn more about each type of stage.

- **User:** Each Snowflake user has a [user stage](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/data-load-local-file-system-create-stage#user-stages) allocated to them by default for file storage. You may find the user stage convenient if your files will only be accessed by a single user, but need to be copied into multiple tables.
- **Named:** A [named stage](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/data-load-local-file-system-create-stage#named-stages) provides high flexibility for data loading. Users with the appropriate privileges on the stage can load data into any table. Furthermore, because the stage is a database object, any security or access rules that apply to all objects will apply to the named stage.

Named stages can be altered and dropped. User stages cannot.

[​](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load#param-named-stage)

Named Stage

drop-down

required

Select your named stage. Read [Creating a named stage](https://docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/data-load-local-file-system-create-stage#creating-a-named-stage) to learn how to create a new named stage.

You can’t select a named stage if its name includes special characters or spaces.

[​](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load#param-load-strategy-1)

Load Strategy

drop-down

- **Append Files in Folder:** Appends files to storage folder. This is the default setting.
- **Overwrite Files in Folder:** Overwrite existing files with matching structure.

[​](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load#param-folder-path)

Folder Path

string

The folder path for the files to be written to. Note that this path follows, but does not include, the bucket or container name.

[​](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load#param-file-prefix)

File Prefix

string

A string of characters that precedes the name of the written files. This can be useful for organizing database objects.

[​](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load#param-storage)

Storage

required

A cloud storage location to load your data into files for storage. Choose either Amazon S3, Azure Storage, or Google Cloud Storage.

- **Databricks:** Load your data into Databricks. You’ll need to set a cloud storage location for temporary staging of the data.

## [​](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load\#fetching-deleted-records)  Fetching deleted records

The Salesforce Load component can fetch deleted records as part of a pipeline run—it does not continuously sync deletions. Deleted records are available while they remain in Salesforce’s Recycle Bin: 15 days by default, or up to 30 days when extended retention is enabled in Salesforce Classic. Deleted rows arrive with `IsDeleted` set to `TRUE`. Remove or soft-delete these rows in your target table downstream—for example, using a `MERGE` on the primary key. To handle deletions more frequently, schedule your pipeline at your required cadence.The Salesforce Load connector supports fetching “deleted” records from Salesforce. To fetch these records in **Basic** mode, add the following in the **Data Source Filter** property:

- Input Column: IsDeleted
- Qualifier: Is
- Comparator: Equal to
- Value: true

To fetch “deleted” records using **Advanced** mode, use the following query:

```
GETDELETED
FROM ${object_name}
where systemmodstamp > '${sub_30daysago}'
```

This advanced query will error when sampling the component. For the advanced query to run successfully, users must run the orchestration pipeline.

When you fetch deleted records, Salesforce returns both live rows (`IsDeleted = FALSE`) and tombstone rows (`IsDeleted = TRUE`, with a `SystemModstamp` value reflecting when the record was deleted). The component loads all returned rows into your staging table.

The Salesforce Load component is read-only. It loads rows into your staging table but does not delete or modify any rows in your data warehouse target. Reconciling deletions in your target table is a downstream step that you control.

### [​](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load\#handling-deleted-records-in-your-target-table)  Handling deleted records in your target table

Use a downstream Transformation pipeline that reads `IsDeleted` from the staging table to reconcile your target table. Two approaches are available:

#### [​](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load\#apply-hard-deletes-to-the-target-table)  Apply hard deletes to the target table

Delete rows from the target table where `Id` matches a staging row with `IsDeleted = TRUE`, then upsert the remaining rows. Records deleted in Salesforce are removed from your data warehouse.

#### [​](https://docs.maia.ai/docs/components/salesforce-load\#apply-soft-deletes-to-the-target-table-recommended)  Apply soft deletes to the target table (recommended)

Instead of physically removing rows, MERGE the `IsDeleted` flag and a `deleted_at` timestamp (sourced from `SystemModstamp`) back onto the target row. The record remains in your data warehouse, preserving an audit trail of what was deleted and when.

Soft delete is the recommended approach for warehouse pipelines. It retains a full audit trail and avoids permanently losing historical data.

With incremental load, a record deleted in Salesforce appears with `IsDeleted = TRUE` in the next pipeline run because its `SystemModstamp` advances past the high-water mark. Your downstream MERGE or DELETE step keeps the target continuously in sync without requiring a full reload.
